column8: Wed 18 Nov: store and 3e's caveat: any arts closure rate needs its definition beside it (Hager's exits only stopped filing); serves no part alone, guards whichever row is quoted.
Wed 18 Nov: store: exit rates by art form; that a residency sits nearer museums than troupes is Keel inference, since residencies are no type in the data.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a evidence guard: the full text corrects store Q9-014's abstract reading (ratios predict exit only by art form), so the report never says thin money predicts closure as a law.
Wed 18 Nov: store: survivors' equity 0.82 vs 0.29 of revenue (about 2.8 times, Keel arithmetic); means across types that row 3 splits, and equity is the group's own, not a founder's bonds.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Bowen et al. read through Hager, period basis unclear; never quoted until read at source.
Wed 18 Nov: store: textbook ratios; the use overclaims, since $50,000 a year is a base, not the whole budget (H9-119): say the shock is kept from the part of the running money her payments cover.

Wed 18 Nov: Green et al. say so (checked at source), but their chance figures are for exactly one flag (41% = 4 x 0.2 x 0.8^3); at least one by chance is 59% (Keel arithmetic), so never close to chance; keep only that the flags are relative.
Wed 18 Nov: store base rate: 3.5% of US charities dissolved in ten years; dissolved means stopped filing, so beside row 1's caveat only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a candidate aha (surplus does not keep a place alive); abstract confirms diversification helps, the 1.0000 not seen: check the margin's units and significance and say no measurable effect; diversification argues for several sources, so bridge to Laura only through Green's grant finding, as Keel inference.
Wed 18 Nov: store, beside row 26: risk falls with age across all charities; row 17 says age protects arts groups less, so never alone.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a and 3d evidence (checked at source): closed UK charities took 60% of income from grants, survivors under 25%; money someone else can withdraw is the danger; 50 closed charities only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a: Green's six months is whole-budget cover from the charity's own assets, the 120 months is her $50,000 share only, so compare on store Q135-031's basis (120 x s), never 120 against six; $445,655 matches NUMBERS 8h.
Wed 18 Nov: same quote as store Q9-015 (abstract); lift Q9-015's source to the full text and add the proxy-effect point there.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e's honest limit: stable grants fail when they end, so what follows 2042 is the residency's and co-sponsors' to plan; the grant-period quote checked at source, the fail sentence is Green's reading, so attribute it to Green et al.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 1's definition caveat; its 37 of 73 is row 16's panel (Hager 1999 there, 2000 here).
Wed 18 Nov: store: one city panel, 37 of 229 closed in about fifteen years (16%, Keel arithmetic); half the exits were not deaths.
Wed 18 Nov: store: age protects arts groups less (7 of 37 arts exits, small numbers); tempers rows 10 and 26.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3.0: managers' order money, size, people; the use overclaims: losing a founding director is about who runs the place, which the plan does not answer; say the payments do not rest on her income.
Wed 18 Nov: store: one case, founder exit; never quote the visionary-leaders line anywhere near Laura; the plan does not cover who runs the residency.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the field's standard list of six killers, abstract only.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e limit beside row 14: young places live on their first money and face a liability of adolescence when it ends; abstract only, so verify before use.
Wed 18 Nov: store and 3e caveat: 19 replacements plus 26 mergers is 45, not 47 (source checked: Nineteen and 26 as stated); give the two counts and drop 47 until Figure 18's labels are confirmed.
Wed 18 Nov: store and Taiwan facts: fills Q9c-023's timeline; founding year differs by source (Res Artis 2007).

Wed 18 Nov: the quoted text says the new operator kept three houses open for exhibitions and resident artists, so the residency was handed on, not plainly ended, and the city's reason is unknown: never ended over its site or the third case where the site decided.
Wed 18 Nov: store: IPS l.15's building is the facility contribution, not upkeep, so never quote it for a site's running costs; that artists' use loses out is Keel inference.

Wed 18 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, checked at source: museums are far more likely to close in their first decade, the decade the ten cover if the residency opens in 2033; verifies store Q9-017; never usually close within ten years; museums, not residencies.

Wed 18 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, quote checked at source; the ten answer funding cuts, not rising costs (fixed nominal $50,000, NUMBERS 8d), and the report says rising costs were independents' commonest trigger: say the half it answers, rising costs to 3e.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or 3d, checked at source: loss of premises the recurrent second cause, the facility's and co-sponsors' job; in Taiwan say two of the cases (Q9c), not every one, since row 24 is unproven.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a evidence, checked at source: private museums closed mostly on life events, owners dying without making provision; differs from store Q9-016 (art museums, closures financial), so name each population.

Wed 18 Nov: store: the report gives 0.5% in its summary and 0.7% (private 2.6%) in its body, so about a quarter to a fifth; independent includes the National Trust, so never say a co-sponsored residency looks like them.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d or 3e, checked at source: thirty museums with 50,000-100,000 visits closed; say the plan puts the ten first, not the case.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3d: a three-year grant paying about 90% is a cliff; a near-death, since it reopened, so never a closure.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a and 3d, checked at source: the reverse order (building first, bought from art sales; running money hoped for; the stock market's wobble among the causes); opened 2018, so about five years, beside the paper's six-year run.
Wed 18 Nov: same case as row 33; the founder's own words and Lumberyard enrich it, one case in the report.
Wed 18 Nov: store: upkeep plus a shrinking grant ended a 23-year place; more arts centre than residency.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e honest limit beside row 33: money without a safe site closed and a site without money closed; the plan answers one death, not every death; drop the New York listing, which serves nothing.
Wed 18 Nov: store and 3e caveat: the field body has no clean count of residency deaths, so the report quotes none.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: cancellations, not closures; store Q9b-017 is survey I.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d: Japan's state residency money fell 60% without notice; a blog's report, and programmes kept growing, so a promise that changed, never a closure cause; never Taiwan.
Wed 18 Nov: store, under row 44: Japan's seed money ran three to five years and most programmes outlived it.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the family placed the site, not shown the money (its size not found), so drop and the money and the likeness to Laura's order.
Wed 18 Nov: store: repairs paused a founder-funded residency; the founder's sum is Wikipedia's only.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: by its own column not evidence either way.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d: co-sponsors know public money promised one to five years at a time, hers ten and owned by the meetings; near the In Taiwan a promise fades reserve and store Q135-034; Auchindrain's three years were paid, not promised.

Wed 18 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, refreshing the founder-run-places reserve: the row says it avoids the founder killer while its own column says it covers one of three; say it answers money that stops (her income included) and leaves the site and who runs the place to others; say the sources read, not every source.
